payload_decode_metadata.scope: Seven representative original gzip payloads versus Zstandard19 of identical decoded SHA256 and bytes. Resident compressed memory and actual decoded output hash, seven alternating trials after equal warmup. Excludes process/native GUI/filesystem/cache publication/whole startup. Compression size CLI audit encodeseconds were recorded during other builds and are not a performance benchmark.

production_runtime.scope: Actual native production executable with staged Zstandard resources in a temporary bundle-like directory; no installation, no GUI, no sealed-app signature claim or Intel-app execution claim.
production_runtime.timing_scope: Process startup plus requested CLI initialization; first use has an empty app payload cache; OS filesystem cache is uncontrolled; native codesign checks occur after measured CLI calls.
timing_limitations: Single verification run per phase; not a before/after startup performance comparison.
The wrapper hashes the compressed archives before CLI execution; first use means an empty application payload cache, not a cold operating-system filesystem cache.
The runtime-first-use phase follows tool initialization in the same scratch HOME; PDFium/fonts are new at that point while the six tool cache files already exist.
The temporary scratch executable and private HOME were removed after verification; original binary and staged resources were retained unchanged.

profiling_rust_tests.note: Before final Files visibility relocation; that change and its new semantic test passed the final default suite.

limitations: Component measurements do not measure whole-app FPS or preview readiness.
Native startup is warm-filesystem, fresh-process/editor-state readiness, not screen presentation. Variability prevents a reliable overall startup speedup claim.

No concurrent builds during matched performance measurements. Native behavioral journeys ran separately from performance measurements; a production build was allowed concurrently with those semantic interaction checks.
Only the ARM production app ran; both architectures of the packaged helper tools were separately executed, with Intel via Rosetta. No sealed universal app or Intel host launch claim.
The 41.27 MiB saving is packaged resources only; matched thin ARM development executable grew 82,832 bytes.
No new per-frame timers, workers or idle repaints. Cache invalidation and bounded decoder work have deterministic regression coverage.
